functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans produce thrust; in: fuel at inlet pressure, throttle command (§5.1.4); out: thrust. Independent per engine — continue after loss of any one engine at/after V1 (§5.1.3).
functions.funcDef: Generate and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1: 'provide thrust for all phases of flight').

functions.subDef: Two inboard engines provide reverse thrust; in: reverse command, WOW+RA agreement (§5.1.2); out: deceleration. Inhibited in flight; separable from forward-thrust generation (§5.1.2).
functions.funcDef: Generate and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subName: Provide reverse thrust on the ground

functions.subDef: Trimmable stabiliser with elevators; in: inceptor/autopilot command, air+inertial data (§5.3.4); out: pitch moment. Elevators on HYD A and C; mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim (§5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers; in: inceptor/autopilot command (§5.3.4); out: roll moment. Ailerons on HYD B and C (§5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with own actuation and hydraulic supply (upper←A, lower←B); sizes to outboard-engine-out at V1 with max blade (§5.3.2/§5.3.3). Segments fail independently; lower has mechanical reversion.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps (four sections) and full-span slats via two independent PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2); out: high-lift position to performance computation.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Nose unit and six main bogies (20 tyres); flotation sized for semi-prepared strip (§5.6.2); in: HYD A retraction/extension with free-fall alternate (§5.6.2); out: gear position, WOW.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, absorb loads, spread footprint pressure, and provide braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support and roll on the surface
functions.funcName: Support the aircraft on the ground and decelerate

functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc, normal from HYD B, alternate HYD A, accumulator-supported emergency (§5.6.2); anti-skid per wheel pair; sizing case 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m rollout (§5.6.3). Independent of extension path.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, provide braking and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Support the aircraft on the ground and decelerate

functions.subDef: Hydraulic steering from tillers and rudder pedals with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2); independent capability from braking (separate harnesses §5.6.5).
functions.funcDef: Provide directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Support the aircraft on the ground and decelerate

functions.subDef: Upward-hinging visor driven by HYD A with electric backup (§5.7.2); in: crew/ground command; out: door position. Cannot operate in flight (§5.7.6).
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access to the full hold length via the nose visor and form the pressure boundary when closed (SDD §5.7.1). Structural load path excluded — treated as structure per §5.7.3.
functions.subName: Open and close the nose visor

functions.subDef: Twelve latches on common torque shaft, eight independent pins on a separate supply; dual dissimilar lock sensing; pressure interlock <0.1 psi (§5.7.2); out: lock status to take-off config monitor. Independent of visor drive.
functions.funcDef: Secure the nose visor and confirm lock integrity (SDD §5.7).

functions.subDef: Nine saddles, two tension straps each, electric winches locked mechanically; loss of one strap carried by neighbours (§5.8.3); in: WOW, loading plan; out: strap tension to flight deck. Lateral/vertical restraint by saddle geometry.
functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade up to 72.6 t along the full hold length through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1). Hold floor hard points excluded — no redundancy, treated as structure (§5.8.3).

functions.subDef: Single instrumented tension loop over every strap; annunciates loss on any strap, and two adjacent stations as a restraint condition (§5.8.2). Coverage is a recorded single-run item (§5.8.3).
functions.funcDef: Monitor restraint integrity in flight (SDD §5.8.2).

functions.subDef: Two air-cycle packs on bleed via cross-bleed manifold, either pack from either side; flight deck and hold separate conditioning zones (§5.9.2); in: bleed, ram air; out: conditioned air.
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold, and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).

functions.subDef: Two digital controllers driving two outflow valves (either sufficient), pneumatic backup, independent mechanical relief (§5.9.2); out: differential/cabin altitude to avionics, oxygen logic, nose-door interlock. Independent of air conditioning.
functions.funcDef: Control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).

functions.subDef: Wing leading edges and engine cowls by hot bleed (piccolo); stabiliser leading edges electrically heated in six independent zones (§5.10.2); out: zone health to avionics. Bleed and electric zones fail independently.
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion is unacceptable, for the icing envelope of the cert basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect airframe surfaces and inlets from ice

functions.subDef: Probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors electrically heated and monitored individually; two detectors of same type on opposite sides (§5.10.2); out: ice detection advisory. Commonality of detector type recorded (§5.10.3).
functions.funcDef: Protect probes and detect icing (SDD §5.10.1).

functions.subDef: Four display units and two HUDs on three display processors over dual networks; three ADIRUs; independent standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing (§5.11.2); out: displays to crew.
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Present flight, navigation and system information

functions.subDef: Alerting consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, on two independent processing channels (§5.11.2); out: alerts to crew. Independent of display presentation.
functions.funcDef: Consolidate and prioritise crew alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Alert the crew to failures and procedures

functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU (AND logic, degrading to single-loop); bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat; hold smoke detection at nine stations (§5.12.2); out: warnings to alerting.
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed to either nacelle; single dedicated APU bottle auto-discharged unattended (§5.12.2); in: fire handle command, hot battery bus power; out: discharge status. Hold has no suppression (§5.12.2).
functions.funcDef: Extinguish or suppress detected fire (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two HP cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feeding four quick-donning demand-regulated masks; either cylinder capable at reduced reserve (§5.13.2/§5.13.3); in: crew donning; out: oxygen to four stations. No passenger oxygen — hold unoccupied.
functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and the following descent/diversion (SDD §5.13.1).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change without crew command (malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Aircraft experiences a thrust excursion not commanded by the crew; trajectory/speed disturbance whose magnitude and symmetry are not bounded by the provided function definition.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded change and intervene to restore intended thrust and trajectory.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the function definition does not state whether the uncommanded change is single-engine or multi-engine, its magnitude, or the resulting speed/trajectory margin, so the aircraft effect (and worst applicable phase) cannot be sized. Needs the bounded thrust-excursion magnitude and affected-engine count to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to crew command (malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Commanded thrust is delivered incorrectly (wrong level or direction of change relative to command); mismatch between intended and actual thrust disturbs the flight path.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the mismatch against expected response and re-commands or reverts to manual thrust management.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the definition does not bound the magnitude of the erroneous response, whether one or multiple engines are affected, or the speed/trajectory margin lost, so the aircraft outcome cannot be sized. Needs the error magnitude and number of engines affected.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric thrust across the aircraft (malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Lateral/directional upset from a thrust asymmetry; the outboard-engine case at the 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing condition against which rudder authority is dimensioned.
fha.effCrew: Crew applies rudder/aileron to hold heading and track; workload rises with asymmetry magnitude, most demanding at low speed in take-off/landing.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class: severity depends on the asymmetry magnitude (which engine, single vs. multiple) versus available rudder authority and the low-speed phase controllability margin, none of which the provided function definition quantifies. The SDD gives the sizing arm but not the margin-vs-authority outcome. Needs the directional-control margin at the sizing asymmetry to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slowly developing thrust asymmetry below crew detection threshold (crew unaware) (malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: A gradually growing lateral/directional bias develops without a crew alert; because the crew take no corrective action, the asymmetry accumulates and can reach a directional-control demand at the sizing moment arm before it is recognised.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action regarding the undetected asymmetry; recognition, if any, is late, compressing the time available to intervene.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class: the effect turns on how large the asymmetry can grow before other cues (heading/track drift, trim) prompt recognition, and on the resulting control margin at that point — the function definition bounds neither. Needs the maximum undetected asymmetry and the residual directional-control margin to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Gradual thrust degradation below crew detection threshold (crew unaware) (malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Slowly reducing available thrust without a crew alert; because the crew take no action, performance/speed margin erodes progressively and may be insufficient when demanded (e.g. climb gradient, go-around).
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally, unaware of the shortfall; the deficit becomes apparent only when demanded thrust is not achieved, compressing available reaction time.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only (hold unoccupied in flight).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class: severity depends on the rate and extent of the undetected thrust loss versus the speed/performance margin (including take-off and go-around cases), which the provided function definition does not quantify. Needs the bounded degradation magnitude/rate and affected-engine count to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust generation (reduced thrust available from one or more of the four engines)
fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust available; on a single-engine failure the aircraft continues to a suitable aerodrome per the design dispatch case, with asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m arm setting the directional-control demand and requiring rudder to trim.
fha.effCrew: Crew identify the affected engine, apply engine-out procedure, manage asymmetry and re-plan to a suitable aerodrome; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-engine loss is within the design dispatch case (continue to a suitable aerodrome) with increased crew workload and reduced thrust margin — a significant reduction in functional capability / significant crew workload, not a large reduction in safety margin. Loss of a second engine on the same side is stated as outside the design dispatch case and retained for study; if that deeper degradation is folded into this condition the class would rise, so confirm the scope. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation (all four engines)
fha.effAc: No propulsive thrust available from any engine; loss of the aircraft's forward-thrust function, forcing a power-off glide with no means of arresting descent to a suitable aerodrome.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an unpowered approach and forced landing; extreme workload with no thrust available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of propulsive thrust from all four engines removes the aircraft's ability to sustain flight and reach a suitable landing site — normally results in loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment in flight (inboard engine reverser)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded in-flight reverser deployment on an inboard engine produces sudden asymmetric drag/thrust and a decelerating, yawing upset; reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only and deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock, so this condition presumes defeat of those interlocks.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise and counter an abrupt yaw/roll excursion at flight speed; very high workload, potentially exceeding control authority depending on flight phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded in-flight reverser deployment on an inboard engine drives an asymmetric upset the interlocks are specifically designed to prevent; loss of control at speed can result in loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on the ground (reverse commanded/deployed on one side only during the landing roll)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric ground reverse produces a yawing moment during the landing rollout on the semi-prepared strip, degrading directional control at a point where the rollout uses much of the 1,800 m available against a predicted ~1,080 m rollout.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply corrective steering/braking to hold the centreline during rollout; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect stated (ground-roll yaw / directional-control demand on a semi-prepared surface), but the SDD does not quantify the reverse-thrust contribution to the stopping/steering budget or the achievable directional authority against asymmetric reverse; classification needs engineering judgement against the landing-distance basis and steering authority rather than a reached-for value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground reverse thrust (reduced reverse available during the landing roll)
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust deceleration during rollout on the semi-prepared strip; stopping relies more heavily on wheel braking against the 1,800 m requirement versus the ~1,080 m predicted rollout, eroding the stopping margin the design rests on.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply increased braking and manage the rollout; increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect stated (erosion of the stopping margin on the semi-prepared surface), but the SDD does not state how much of the deceleration budget reverse thrust supplies, so the residual stopping margin with reverse degraded cannot be grounded; classification needs the performance/braking data rather than a reached-for value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground reverse thrust
fha.effAc: Deceleration on the operating surface relies on wheel braking alone; predicted rollout ~1,080 m against an 1,800 m landing distance requirement on a semi-prepared surface, so stopping capability is retained but the deceleration margin is reduced.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of reverser unavailability; increased braking demand and reduced margin on the strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reverse thrust supplements wheel braking; with braking retained a significant reduction in the stopping safety margin on a semi-prepared surface — not a total loss of deceleration. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.effAc: Pitch surface moves in a manner inconsistent with the command; an erroneous pitch response can drive the aircraft outside its flight-path or structural limits.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an unexpected pitch response; potential for excessive workload or inability to recover.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous pitch response drives the flight path away from crew intent and can exceed structural/flight-envelope limits leading to loss of the aircraft; consistent with SFHA FC-207. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no command
fha.effAc: Pitch surface moves with no crew or autopilot command; an uncommanded pitch input can drive the aircraft outside its flight-path or structural limits before the crew reacts.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and arrest an unexpected uncommanded motion; potential for excessive workload or inability to recover.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded pitch motion can exceed structural/flight-envelope limits leading to loss of the aircraft; consistent with SFHA FC-208. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slowly developing erroneous pitch response below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Pitch response is erroneous but develops slowly enough to remain below the crew detection threshold; the resulting flight-path deviation accumulates before the crew becomes aware.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action until the deviation becomes detectable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the residual pitch authority, the detection latency, and the flight-path/structural excursion reached before the crew becomes aware — none of these is fixed by the function definition; requires an aware/unaware detection assumption to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch trim runaway below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Trimmable stabiliser runs uncommanded at a rate below the crew detection threshold; trim authority accumulates over time and the out-of-trim condition builds before the crew becomes aware.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action until the out-of-trim condition or control-force change becomes detectable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the runaway rate, the trim authority reachable before detection, and the residual controllability at the resulting mistrim — not established by the function definition; requires a crew-detection and residual-authority assumption to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority within MAC limits
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority; aircraft controllable within centre-of-gravity limits but with degraded manoeuvre/trim margin and reduced ability to counter upsets.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain the flight path with degraded authority; degraded law/failure annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in functional capability / safety margin in pitch, within controllable CG limits — no loss of control stated. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority outside MAC limits
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Pitch authority insufficient to trim/control at CG outside the manoeuvre-controllable band; large reduction in safety margins with the aircraft near the edge of controllability.
fha.effCrew: Excessive workload; crew may be unable to reliably maintain the flight path with the remaining authority.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Outside MAC limits the remaining authority yields a large reduction in safety margins/capability and excessive crew workload, short of complete loss of control. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No means of controlling pitch attitude; loss of the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to control the flight path in pitch.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; loss of the aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of a primary control axis prevents controlled flight — loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Roll response differs from that commanded (wrong sense, magnitude or rate), producing an unintended bank/roll disturbance about the roll axis.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the erroneous response; workload and difficulty depend on magnitude and phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of longitudinal payload restraint at a single station (loss not annunciated; crew continue duties normally)
fha.effAc: Single-station longitudinal restraint lost and carried by neighbours per design load-path sizing; because it is undetected the condition may persist and could progress. Effect on aircraft depends on residual margin and on whether progression to further stations is credible, which the provided material does not quantify.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware: no annunciation, crew continue duties normally and take no action. In-flight adjustment of restraint is not possible in any case.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: SDD states single-strap loss is carried by neighbours, but the UNDETECTED case (monitoring coverage gap) raises the question of undetected progression to a worse state, for which no residual-margin or progression analysis is provided. Need the restraint load-path margin and the tension-loop coverage substantiation to derive an effect and classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint (all restraint straps ineffective for the single unitised blade)
fha.effAc: Longitudinal restraint of the single 72.6 t blade occupying the full 108 m hold length is lost. Uncontrolled longitudinal blade movement is credible, driving a centre-of-gravity excursion beyond limits and loss of the payload load path; loss of the airplane is credible.
fha.effCrew: Crew has in-flight indication only and no means to adjust or re-establish restraint; unable to arrest blade movement.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of longitudinal restraint of a single 72.6 t blade over the full hold length permits an uncontrolled CG excursion the crew cannot correct in flight; consistent with loss of the airplane. Proposed for engineer confirmation; the resulting CG excursion magnitude should be substantiated by weight-and-balance / restraint analysis. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous indication of adequate strap tension masking a real restraint loss (monitoring shows tension adequate while restraint is degraded/lost)
fha.effAc: The tension monitoring loop is the only in-flight cue to a restraint condition; an erroneous 'adequate' indication removes crew awareness of a genuine restraint loss, allowing that underlying restraint condition to persist and potentially progress. Aircraft-level effect is that of the masked restraint failure, which the provided material does not quantify.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the real restraint loss: no annunciation, crew continue duties normally and take no action. No in-flight restraint adjustment is available in any case.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold not occupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a standalone severity: this masking condition takes its aircraft effect from the underlying restraint loss it hides, and the restraint residual-margin / progression effects (SF-012 partial and total cases) are themselves not quantified in the provided material. Classify once the masked restraint conditions are substantiated.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of strap-tension monitoring coverage — tension state at one or more stations not instrumented/annunciated while restraint remains physically intact
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft; a subsequent loss of restraint at an un-monitored station would go undetected, removing the crew's cue to act
fha.effCrew: Reduced restraint-state awareness at affected station(s); crew retains monitoring at instrumented stations
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SF-013 is a monitoring function; a coverage gap has no aircraft effect on its own. Severity depends on the coincident restraint-loss condition it would fail to reveal (SF-012, covered separately) and on how many stations lose coverage — that combined case is not stated in the SF-013 definition. Left empty pending that dependency.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of strap-tension monitoring — no station instrumented, no in-flight annunciation of restraint tension
fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft; complete loss of the in-flight cue such that any subsequent restraint slackening or loss at any station would be undetected by the crew
fha.effCrew: Complete loss of in-flight restraint-state awareness; crew has indication only in normal operation and no in-flight adjustment capability
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Monitoring-only function: with restraint physically intact there is no aircraft effect. The safety significance is that a later restraint loss (SF-012) would be undetected; that coincident case, and whether the take-off configuration monitor mitigates on the ground, are not in the SF-013 definition. Left empty pending that dependency.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin and hold air conditioning
fha.effAc: No conditioned air delivered to the flight deck or the hold; pressurisation air supply lost. Flight deck loses temperature/ventilation control; with no bleed conditioning the crew initiates a descent to a level not requiring pressurisation. Hold is unoccupied so hold conditioning loss has no occupant effect.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing an unconditioned flight deck and executing a precautionary descent/diversion; crew oxygen available for any associated pressurisation effect.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of flight-deck conditioning with a descent and crew-oxygen backstop is a significant increase in crew workload with no occupants affected. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous commanded cabin differential
fha.effAc: Pressurisation controller drives an incorrect differential; cabin/hold pressure diverges from intended. Excursion is bounded by independent mechanical positive/negative relief protecting the structure; crew intervenes via manual mode. Potential cabin-altitude excursion pending confirmation of the magnitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the erroneous differential from cabin-altitude indication and alerting, reverts to manual control, and dons oxygen if cabin altitude climbs; increased workload during recovery.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: On the crew-aware assumption, an erroneous differential toward structural relief is a large reduction in safety margins recoverable with crew action and oxygen; the exact cabin-altitude excursion is not quantified in the SDD, so confirm against the pressurisation schedule. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded change in cabin pressure with no selection
fha.effAc: Cabin/hold pressure changes with no crew selection; excursion bounded by independent mechanical relief. Crew reverts to manual mode to arrest the change.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware from cabin-altitude/rate indication and alerting, selects manual mode and dons oxygen if cabin altitude rises; increased workload during recovery.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: On the crew-aware assumption an uncommanded pressure excursion toward relief is a large reduction in safety margins recoverable with crew action and oxygen; the excursion magnitude is not quantified in the SDD, so confirm. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow drift of cabin pressure below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Cabin pressure drifts undetected; with the crew unaware they take no action and continue duties normally. Cabin altitude climbs progressively toward the point where crew performance and consciousness are affected before mechanical relief or oxygen arming intervenes.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties, does not detect the drift, and does not don oxygen; potential creeping degradation of crew performance if cabin altitude reaches an incapacitating level.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Class depends on the cabin-altitude ceiling the slow drift can reach undetected and on the crew-oxygen arming/alerting altitude relative to that ceiling; the SDD gives max altitude FL260 and a preliminary ~8,800 m hold equivalent but does not quantify the achievable undetected cabin-altitude excursion or the oxygen arming logic. Missing: the detection/alert threshold, the drift ceiling, and the automatic oxygen provisioning altitude. Abstain until provided.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic control with manual mode available
fha.effAc: Automatic pressurisation control lost; crew reverts to the available manual mode, with a pneumatic backup driving one outflow valve and independent mechanical relief still protecting the structure. Pressure control maintained by crew at increased attention.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in workload managing pressurisation manually for the remainder of the flight; fallback modes annunciated and available.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of automatic control with a manual mode, pneumatic backup and independent relief still available is a slight increase in crew workload with margins preserved. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of airframe/inlet ice protection — loss of protection on one or more surface zones
fha.effAc: Ice may accrete on the unprotected zone(s) in icing conditions; aerodynamic and/or inlet performance degraded on the affected surface, with the consequence dependent on which zone (wing LE, cowl, stabiliser, or probe) is lost.
fha.effCrew: Lost electrical zone is annunciated; crew assumed to exit icing and manage the affected zone per procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect cannot be classified from the function definition alone: severity depends on WHICH zone is lost (a wing/inlet loss differs materially from a single stabiliser zone or probe) and on the icing severity encountered — not resolvable without engineering judgement on the affected-surface set and the exposure.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced environmental pack capacity from bleed anti-ice demand while ice protection is in use
fha.effAc: Bleed drawn for wing/cowl anti-ice reduces available pack capacity; conditioning schedule reduced while anti-ice is active. Ice protection itself remains available.
fha.effCrew: Performance penalty of wing anti-ice is applied automatically to displayed performance; crew manage conditioning schedule.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight-deck conditioning reduced but maintained.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced conditioning schedule with ice protection retained is at most a slight increase in crew workload / physical discomfort, not a reduction in safety margin. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ice-detection advisory (false or missed)
fha.effAc: A false advisory may command/permit unnecessary anti-ice (a bleed/pack penalty); a missed advisory in automatic mode may leave protection off while ice accretes. Detection is advisory and the system may be selected on manually at any time.
fha.effCrew: Crew may act on a false advisory, or fail to activate protection in automatic on a missed advisory; manual selection remains available at any time.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the definition alone: the aircraft effect of a missed vs false advisory hinges on whether the crew is in automatic reliance or would independently select ice protection, and on the accretion actually occurring — a mitigation/exposure judgement the function definition does not settle.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure of icing detection (missed accretion)
fha.effAc: Detection function fails without annunciation; in automatic mode ice protection is not commanded and accretion proceeds undetected until effects manifest through handling or performance.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware of the detection failure; no protective action taken unless ice effects become independently apparent.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the definition alone: severity of a latent detection loss depends on whether protection would be manually/automatically selected regardless, on the two-detector commonality, and on the icing actually encountered — none resolvable without engineering judgement on the mitigation path and exposure.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of individual probe heating — heating fails on one probe with no annunciation, crew continue normally
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Function definition 'Heat probes and detect icing' names the lost capability but the SDD does not establish which probe channels are affected or the redundancy of the parameter each probe serves; without the resulting effect on displayed air data validity and whether a single undetected probe-heat loss can produce misleading data, the aircraft/crew effect cannot be stated and severity cannot be derived. Needs: probe-to-parameter mapping and data-integrity architecture.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of heating on one or more probes, static ports or windshields — heated elements unpowered on a subset
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states probes/ports/windshields are electrically heated and monitored individually, and lost zones are annunciated, but does not establish the redundancy of each affected air-data parameter or whether loss of heating on a given element produces erroneous versus lost data. Without the downstream effect on air-data validity the aircraft/crew effect and severity cannot be derived. Needs: element-to-parameter mapping and voting/monitoring architecture.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of icing detection and probe heating — no detection and no heated protection of probes/ports/windshields
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss removes both icing awareness and probe/port/windshield protection, so in icing conditions air-data sensing could degrade; but the SDD does not establish the air-data integrity/monitoring that would determine whether this yields lost or misleading data, nor the exposure model for encountering icing after the loss. The aircraft effect (and therefore severity) cannot be derived from the function definition alone. Needs: air-data monitoring architecture and icing-encounter exposure basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Misleading flight, navigation or system information presented and undetected by the crew
fha.effAc: Aircraft flown to erroneous flight/navigation reference with no crew cross-check triggered; potential departure from intended flightpath/envelope. Independent standby instrument (DC ESS, shares no supply/sensor/processing) available to expose a discrepancy only if the crew cross-checks it.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on false information believing it valid; no alert or discrepancy flagged, so detection depends on manual cross-check against the standby.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary flight/navigation information can drive the aircraft outside the flight envelope with the crew unaware; consistent with existing FC-269 classification for this condition. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary display presentation with standby instrument retained
fha.effAc: Primary display presentation lost; independent standby attitude/airspeed/altitude on DC essential remains available to continue flight and land.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload flying on the reduced standby presentation; loss of primary formats and HUD.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Retained independent standby presentation preserves means to continue and land at significantly increased workload; consistent with existing FC-271 classification. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one or more display formats or reference sources
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Function definition and SDD do not fix how much presentation/reference redundancy remains for a given 'one or more' loss (three display processors, three ADIRUs, any-DU-any-format, dual networks). The aircraft-level effect ranges from reversion-only workload to a larger degradation depending on which formats/sources are lost; cannot ground a single aircraft effect or class. Needs the specific format/source-loss set and remaining reconfiguration to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight, navigation and system information display
fha.effAc: All primary display presentation lost; independent standby instrument (attitude/airspeed/altitude, DC essential, no shared supply/sensor/processing) provides a degraded means to continue flight and land.
fha.effCrew: Large reduction in available information and a large increase in workload; crew fly on standby attitude/airspeed/altitude only, with loss of navigation and system information presentation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary display with only the independent standby retained is a large reduction in functional capability and a large workload increase, short of loss of the aircraft; consistent with existing FC-270 classification. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Spurious or nuisance alerting presented to the crew
fha.effAc: No actual failure exists; alerting presents false warnings/procedures. Potential for crew to action an unnecessary procedure or be distracted from primary tasks.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload diagnosing and dismissing false alerts and confirming true aircraft state; risk of desensitisation to genuine alerts.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Nuisance alerting produces a significant increase in crew workload with no genuine failure present; consistent with existing FC-273 classification. Confirm against the alerting HMI and workload assessment. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate an existing failure condition (missed alert) — an active failure elsewhere on the aircraft is not presented to the crew
fha.effAc: An existing system failure remains unmitigated because no alert is raised; the aircraft continues in a degraded state whose driving condition is unknown to the crew.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware of the failure and take no corrective or procedural action; discovery, if any, is delayed and indirect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Missed annunciation defeats the crew's means of detecting and managing an existing failure, a large reduction in functional capability and the crew's ability to cope with an adverse condition. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Incorrect or misleading procedure presented for the condition — an alert is raised but the associated procedure is wrong for the actual failure
fha.effAc: Crew act on a procedure inappropriate to the true condition, potentially aggravating the failure or configuring the aircraft adversely.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute the presented (wrong) procedure believing it correct; correct management of the real condition is not performed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A misleading procedure presented as authoritative can drive incorrect crew action against a real failure, a large reduction in safety margins / functional capability. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one alerting processing channel — one of two independent processing channels lost, alerting retained on the remaining channel
fha.effAc: Alerting function retained on the surviving channel; loss of channel redundancy only, no loss of alerting capability.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload/awareness of degraded redundancy; alerting remains available for the flight.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Alerting is driven by two independent processing channels; loss of one leaves the function intact on the other, a slight reduction in margin only. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of alert prioritisation/consolidation with basic alerts retained — individual alerts still presented but no longer ranked or consolidated
fha.effAc: Alerts remain available but unprioritised/unconsolidated; the aircraft state is annunciated but the driving condition is harder to identify among concurrent alerts.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload to sort and identify the governing condition without consolidation/prioritisation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Basic alerting retained but loss of the prioritisation/consolidation that manages concurrent alerts imposes a significant increase in crew workload. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting and associated procedures — no failure of any system is annunciated to the crew and no procedures are presented
fha.effAc: No system failure anywhere on the aircraft is annunciated; the aircraft may accumulate undetected failures with no procedural guidance available.
fha.effCrew: Crew lose the primary means of learning what has failed and what to do; detection and management of all subsequent failures degraded to direct-indication and airmanship.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of the function that tells the crew what has failed and what to do is a large reduction in functional capability and crew ability to cope; the SDD gives no basis to assert loss of alerting alone is unsurvivable, so Catastrophic is not stated. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Spurious fire/overheat warning presented to the crew with no actual fire or overheat (malfunction of detect fire and overheat)
fha.effAc: No actual hazard exists; aircraft remains fully controllable. A spurious engine/APU fire warning may prompt a precautionary engine shutdown or extinguishant discharge, degrading available thrust/redundancy for the remainder of the flight.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to diagnose and disposition a warning that does not correspond to a real condition; potential unnecessary application of the fire drill and diversion decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Spurious warning with no real hazard, but a credible unnecessary engine shutdown/diversion on a four-engine freighter is a significant increase in crew workload and a significant reduction in functional capability for the remaining sector. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of hold smoke detection at one or more stations (latent malfunction of detect fire and overheat)
fha.effAc: One or more of the nine hold smoke-detection stations inoperative and undetected; reduced smoke-detection coverage over the hold length. Hold carries a single unitised blade with no suppression fitted; a hold smoke source at an unmonitored station would not be annunciated.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the coverage loss; continue normal duties.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity from the function definition alone: the aircraft-level effect of an undetected hold smoke event depends on the substantiation of the 'detection but no suppression' decision (recorded as an assumption in the SDD) and on how many of the nine stations are lost — neither is established here. Leave for engineering judgement against the hold-fire hazard.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection (no monitored zone — engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, gear bays, hold — provides fire or overheat annunciation to the crew)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No means to detect a fire or overheat in any monitored zone; an initiating fire progresses undetected, defeating timely crew isolation/extinguishing and threatening the airframe
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no fire/overheat warning; unable to initiate the fire drill for an existing fire; increased exposure to an undetected developing fire
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of the crew's ability to detect a fire/overheat across all monitored zones is a large reduction in safety margin/functional capability with an undetected fire progressing; effects support Hazardous. A step to Catastrophic requires the combined event of an actual undetected fire, which is a fault-tree contribution, not the FHA top effect. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge with no fire (a bottle discharges into a nacelle when no fire or overheat is present)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One extinguisher bottle depleted with no fire present; the second cross-plumbed bottle of the pair remains available, so extinguishing capability for that engine pair is degraded but retained
fha.effCrew: Nuisance discharge indication; crew workload to assess and dispatch; possible unnecessary engine shutdown
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no occupants in hold
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed, an inadvertent single-bottle discharge leaves the redundant bottle available; the effect is a significant increase in crew workload and loss of one extinguishing shot rather than loss of the function. Effects support Major. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to discharge on crew command (crew commands extinguisher discharge for an engine/APU fire and no extinguishant is delivered)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A commanded fire cannot be suppressed by the demanded bottle; an engine/APU fire may continue uncontrolled, threatening the affected zone and adjacent structure/systems
fha.effCrew: Crew execute the fire drill but the fire is not suppressed; must resort to the second cross-plumbed bottle where applicable; high workload managing an uncontained fire
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no occupants in hold
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Failure to suppress a commanded, detected engine/APU fire is a large reduction in safety margin. Cross-plumbing provides a second bottle for the engine pair, which supports Hazardous rather than Catastrophic; confirm whether the demanded-bottle failure can propagate to loss of both bottles of the pair, which would drive the classification higher. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing to one engine zone (extinguishant cannot be delivered to one nacelle of an engine pair)
fha.phases: Taxi, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Extinguishing capability to one nacelle is reduced; because either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair, protection to that zone may still be available through the cross-plumbed path, so the effect is a partial degradation with margin retained
fha.effCrew: Crew retain a means to address a fire in the affected engine pair via the cross-plumbed bottle; some increase in workload/assessment
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no occupants in hold
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Cross-plumbing means loss of extinguishing to a single engine zone is a partial reduction of the extinguishing capability with a redundant delivery path retained; effects support a significant reduction in margin/capability short of Hazardous. Confirm the failure that removes delivery to one zone does not simultaneously block the cross-plumbed path. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of APU fire extinguishing capability — the single dedicated APU bottle unavailable to discharge, with engine-pair extinguishing retained
fha.effAc: An APU compartment fire cannot be extinguished by the fixed system; per the SDD the APU bottle is discharged automatically on detection with the aircraft unattended, so the loss removes the primary suppression for an APU-zone fire. APU detection remains and APU shutdown/fuel isolation on APU fire remains. Extinguishing for the four engine nacelles is unaffected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the aircraft effect of an unextinguished APU fire depends on APU compartment fire containment, the effect of automatic APU shutdown/fuel isolation, and whether the fire propagates beyond the APU fire zone — none of which is stated at function level. Provide the APU-fire propagation/containment case and expected duration before committing a class; do not default to a benign value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing capability — no fixed extinguishant available to any engine nacelle or the APU compartment
fha.effAc: No fixed means to extinguish or suppress a fire in any engine nacelle or the APU compartment; fire detection and crew alerting are retained, and shutdown/fuel isolation of an affected engine or the APU remains available, but an established fire in a monitored fire zone cannot be extinguished by the aircraft system. Only portable extinguishers at the flight deck and hold access door remain, which do not reach the nacelles.
fha.effCrew: Crew are alerted to the fire and can shut down and isolate the affected engine/APU via the fire handle, but have no means to extinguish the fire in the nacelle.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The condition is loss of extinguishing ONLY; its aircraft effect is realised only in coincidence with an actual fire, whose severity depends on fire growth, structural/systems damage and propagation not stated at function level. A committed class requires the concurrent-fire case (probability of a fire that would otherwise have been extinguished, and its consequence) — that is a combined-condition assessment. Leave empty rather than assume the fire case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded crew-oxygen flow or leakage — oxygen discharged or leaking without crew demand, depleting the stored supply
fha.effAc: Oxygen is drawn down without crew demand, reducing the reserve available for a subsequent depressurisation, smoke/fume event and the ensuing descent and diversion; a thermal discharge indicator on the skin shows an overboard overpressure discharge. Two cylinders with a crossover mean a single-cylinder leak may be isolable, but an undetected or un-isolated leak erodes the sized four-occupant duration.
fha.effCrew: Crew may receive low-pressure alerting; response is to isolate via the crossover where possible and to manage remaining reserve, increasing workload and constraining any subsequent depressurisation response.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect depends on whether the leak is detected and isolable and on the oxygen duration remaining relative to the diversion time from FL260 — the function definition gives the sizing basis but not the leak-detection/isolation coverage or the coincident-depressurisation exposure needed to fix the class. Provide the leak isolation coverage and the residual-duration-vs-diversion case before committing; do not assume benign.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous crew-oxygen cylinder pressure / status indication reading normal while the true state is degraded (undetected — crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Indication reads normal while the actual oxygen supply is depleted or unavailable; the crew are unaware and take no action, so the deficiency is discovered only when oxygen is demanded — during a loss of pressurisation, smoke or fume event. Crew oxygen may then be inadequate for the descent and diversion for which it is sized. No effect on flight path until the latent condition is exposed.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally, believing oxygen is available; on demanding oxygen in a depressurisation or smoke/fume event they find it insufficient, which can incapacitate or seriously impair the flight crew during a demanding phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is the crew-unaware (latent) case whose worst effect requires coincidence with a depressurisation or smoke/fume event; the resulting severity turns on that combined exposure and on crew incapacitation consequence, which are not established at function level. The pairing with a loss-of-pressurisation condition must be assessed before a class is committed — leave empty rather than assume the coincidence probability.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen — loss of supply to one or more mask stations with remaining stations available
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the airframe; a degraded means of protecting the crew against a depressurisation, smoke or fume event, with fewer mask stations available than the nominal four.
fha.effCrew: Regulators are independent per mask, so loss at one or more stations still leaves protected stations for the nominal two-crew complement; increased workload to manage station allocation and to consider the reserve position. Crew becomes aware via system status/low-pressure alerting.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold is unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With independent per-mask regulators and a nominal complement of two against four mask stations, loss of one or more stations reduces protection margin and increases crew workload during a depressurisation/smoke event but does not by itself deny protected breathing to the operating crew — a significant reduction in safety margin / significant increase in crew workload. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced oxygen reserve / duration developing below the indication threshold — crew unaware
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the airframe; an undetected erosion of the oxygen endurance available to protect the crew for the descent and diversion following a depressurisation, smoke or fume event.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties with no annunciation and plan the diversion on a believed reserve that is not present; if a depressurisation/smoke event then occurs the oxygen may exhaust before the diversion is complete, with incapacitation of the operating crew a credible outcome. Awareness assumption: none — the loss develops below the indication threshold so no crew action is taken.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold is unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected reduction of reserve means the crew plan on protection they do not have; combined with a subsequent depressurisation/smoke event it can lead to depletion during the diversion and crew physical distress or incapacitation impairing task performance. Not classified Catastrophic because it requires the coincident depressurisation/smoke event and two crossover-linked cylinders provide some reserve; engineer to confirm against the diversion-time sizing case and the depressurisation exposure at FL260. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply — no supply available at any mask station
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the airframe; the aircraft is left with no means of protecting the flight crew during a depressurisation, smoke or fume event and the ensuing descent and diversion.
fha.effCrew: On a depressurisation at altitude or a smoke/fume event, the operating crew has no supplemental oxygen; hypoxia or smoke/fume exposure can incapacitate both crew members during the descent/diversion — potential loss of the flight crew and the aircraft. Crew becomes aware via low-pressure/status alerting but cannot restore supply in flight.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold is unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of crew oxygen coincident with a depressurisation or smoke/fume event can incapacitate the entire two-crew complement, credibly leading to loss of the aircraft. Engineer to confirm the coincident-event assumption and the depressurisation exposure given FL260 max operating altitude and the low hold differential. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The four systems the SDD designates as resources (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) and the two structural items (nose-door load path, hold hard points) are correctly excluded from the aircraft function list.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource is intended as an aircraft function, additional top functions and their decompositions would be required.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS and nose-door/hold structure from all add_function actions.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.rationale: The prompt's modeling rule and the SDD both classify these as resources/structure, not functions; I relied on that to omit them.

assumptions.text: Pitch, roll, yaw and high-lift are sub-functions of a single aircraft-level 'Control aircraft trajectory' function rather than separate top-level functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If they belong at aircraft-function level, four separate top functions replace one, changing the AFHA row structure.

citations.quote: provides the control authority required across the flight envelope

assumptions.usedFor: 'Detect fire and overheat' vs 'Extinguish engine and APU fire' sub-functions.

citations.quote: DC power from the essential bus to detection and from the hot battery bus to the discharge circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes distinct hardware and power sources (detection on essential bus, discharge on hot battery bus) but does not state they fail independently.

assumptions.text: For SF-003/004/005 the TL-with-two-partials modelling style is used (complete loss plus within-MAC and outside-MAC degraded partials) rather than TL = loss of minimum acceptable configuration.
assumptions.ifWrong: Partial-loss entries would collapse to a single degraded-mode phrase and the within/outside-MAC split would move to the FHA effects instead.
assumptions.rationale: The provided function list and SDD do not fix which TL modelling convention the programme has adopted for control axes.

assumptions.text: Slowly developing erroneous/uncommanded control-axis and thrust behaviour can progress below crew detection thresholds, justifying the crew-Unaware rows.
assumptions.ifWrong: The crew-Unaware rows for SF-003/004/005 and SF-001 would be removed and those conditions covered on the Aware rows only.

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.text: Crew Indication/Annunciation and Mitigation fields are left empty for these functions because the SDD describes system-level annunciations (degraded-law, jam/asymmetry discretes) but no established aircraft-function-level detection or crew procedure tied to each failure condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: Indication and mitigation cells would be populated from the FCS/PRP operation sections rather than left amber for engineer fill.

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes; high-lift position to the performance computation

assumptions.rationale: Per the abstention rule, indication/mitigation cannot be grounded until effects and detection means are analysed against each specific failure condition.

assumptions.text: High-lift asymmetry and runaway are detected in flight via the asymmetry-brake trip and its annunciation, so the crew-Aware variant applies to the commanded/uncommanded-motion malfunctions.
assumptions.ifWrong: An erroneous/asymmetric high-lift condition that develops undetected would need its own crew-Unaware row and could raise the classification the AFHA later assigns.

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes asymmetry brakes at each section but does not explicitly state a flight-deck annunciation, so the awareness tag for the SF-006 malfunction cell is inferred.

assumptions.ifWrong: If the margin does not absorb the degraded case, the partial-loss braking condition drives a different downstream classification and requirement set.

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts dual dissimilar sensing but gives no coverage evidence that both paths cannot be simultaneously misleading, so an undetected erroneous-indication variant is retained.

assumptions.text: Ground flotation loss (footprint pressure exceeding what the operating surface accepts) is a distinct partial-loss condition of SF-007 separate from a rolling/support loss.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby shares nothing with the primaries but does not state crew procedure or detection thresholds, so detectability of misleading data is inferred.

assumptions.text: A missed alert or missed fire/overheat detection can develop below crew detection thresholds because no independent cue exists once the sensing channel fails silently.
assumptions.ifWrong: If failure monitoring annunciates loss of the alerting/detection channel itself, the missed-alert and missed-detection conditions become crew-Aware, collapsing the Unaware rows for SF-019 and SF-020.

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The SDD grounds the annunciation paths but not the failure-annunciation (monitoring) coverage, so the undetected variants are retained on the Unaware row.

assumptions.text: Hold smoke detection loss at individual stations is not independently annunciated to the crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If station health is monitored the undetected hold-detection-loss condition becomes crew-Aware and moves off the SF-020 Unaware row.

citations.quote: The hold has smoke detection at nine stations along its length and no suppression

assumptions.ifWrong: If a station loss can affect an occupied crew position with no usable alternative, SF-022-PL could rise toward Hazardous.

assumptions.text: SF-022-PL2 is not a distinct condition in the current model and cannot be classified separately from SF-022-PL3.
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM for SF-022 lists only aware SF-022-PL and unaware SF-022-PL3; no PL2 text exists to ground an effect.
assumptions.ifWrong: If PL2 is intended as an aware 'reduced reserve, crew notices via displayed endurance' condition, it would likely classify Major (increased workload, informed diversion) rather than remaining empty.
